title: 04. BM25 & Lexical Search: Tokenisation and Text Preprocessing for BM25
summary: Before a chef can cook, they must prep the ingredients — washing, chopping, removing inedible parts. Raw ingredients can't go straight into the pot. > > BM25 is the chef.

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy
sections.body:
> Before a chef can cook, they must **prep the ingredients** — washing, chopping, removing inedible parts. Raw ingredients can't go straight into the pot.
>
> BM25 is the chef. Your raw text is the ingredient. **Preprocessing** is the prep work — lowercasing, removing stopwords, stemming. If you skip prep, your dish (search results) will be inconsistent and messy.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body:
BM25 treats every unique string as a different word. `"Running"`, `"running"`, and `"RUNNING"` are three different keys in the inverted index — even though they mean the same thing. Preprocessing fixes this by normalising text before it enters the index.

The main preprocessing steps are: lowercase → tokenise → remove stopwords → stem (or lemmatise).

sections.title: ③ Why Does This Matter?
sections.body: Without preprocessing, your BM25 index is fragile: a query for "running" won't match documents about "ran" or "runs". Proper preprocessing dramatically improves recall (finding relevant documents) without hurting precision (avoiding irrelevant ones).

sections.title: ⑤ Beginner-Friendly Code Example
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Step 1: Make everything lowercase
- Step 2: Remove punctuation
- Simple whitespace split
- Regex tokenisation — keeps only alphanumeric words
- LESSON 11: Tokenisation and Text Preprocessing for BM25
- Install: pip install nltk spacy rank-bm25
- STEP 1: The Preprocessing Problems
- STEP 3: Punctuation and Special Character Removal

**Defines:** `step_lowercase()`, `step_remove_punctuation()`, `tokenise_simple()`, `tokenise_regex()`, `remove_stopwords()`, `stem_tokens()`, `full_preprocess_pipeline()`

```python
# ============================================================
# LESSON 11: Tokenisation and Text Preprocessing for BM25
# Install: pip install nltk spacy rank-bm25
# ============================================================

import string
import re

# ── STEP 1: The Preprocessing Problems ───────────────────────────────

raw_texts = [
    "Running Python scripts is EASY!",
    "I ran 3 Python programs yesterday.",
    "She runs the Python environment daily.",
    "The cats are eating the mice.",   # → should match query "cat eat mouse"
    "Machine-learning: best practices for 2024",
]

print("=== THE PREPROCESSING PROBLEM ===")
print("Without preprocessing, these all look DIFFERENT to BM25:")
for text in raw_texts:
    print(f"  '{text.split()}' ← raw tokens")
print()

# ── STEP 2: Lowercasing ───────────────────────────────────────────────

def step_lowercase(text):
    """Step 1: Make everything lowercase"""
    return text.lower()

print("=== STEP 1: Lowercasing ===")
for text in raw_texts[:3]:
    print(f"  Before: '{text}'")
    print(f"  After:  '{step_lowercase(text)}'")
    print()

# ── STEP 3: Punctuation and Special Character Removal ─────────────────

def step_remove_punctuation(text):
    """Step 2: Remove punctuation"""
    # Replace hyphens with spaces (machine-learning → machine learning)
    text = text.replace('-', ' ')
    # Remove all other punctuation
    text = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
    return text

print("=== STEP 2: Remove Punctuation ===")
for text in raw_texts:
    cleaned = step_remove_punctuation(text.lower())
    print(f"  '{text}' → '{cleaned}'")
print()

# ── STEP 4: Tokenisation Strategies ──────────────────────────────────

def tokenise_simple(text):
    """Simple whitespace split"""
    return text.split()

def tokenise_regex(text):
    """Regex tokenisation — keeps only alphanumeric words"""
    # \b[a-z]+\b matches word boundaries around alphabetic sequences
    return re.findall(r'\b[a-z0-9]+\b', text.lower())

print("=== STEP 3: Tokenisation ===")
test = "Machine-learning: best practices for 2024!"
print(f"Input: '{test}'")
print(f"Simple split:  {tokenise_simple(test.lower())}")
print(f"Regex method:  {tokenise_regex(test)}")
print()

# ── STEP 5: Stopword Removal ──────────────────────────────────────────

# Install NLTK stopwords: python -m nltk.downloader stopwords
import nltk
nltk.download('stopwords', quiet=True)
from nltk.corpus import stopwords

# Get English stopwords
stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
print(f"=== STEP 4: Stopword Removal ===")
print(f"Total English stopwords: {len(stop_words)}")
print(f"Sample: {sorted(list(stop_words))[:20]}")
print()

def remove_stopwords(tokens, stop_words):
    """Remove common words that carry no relevance information"""
    return [token for token in tokens if token not in stop_words]

# Example
tokens = tokenise_regex("Python is great for machine learning and data science")
print(f"Before stopword removal: {tokens}")
tokens_no_stop = remove_stopwords(tokens, stop_words)
print(f"After stopword removal:  {tokens_no_stop}")
print()

# IMPORTANT WARNING: when NOT to remove stopwords
print("⚠️  WARNING: Don't always remove stopwords!")
print("   Query 'to be or not to be' → all words are stopwords!")
print("   Query 'not working' → 'not' changes meaning completely!")
print()

# ── STEP 6: Stemming ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

from nltk.stem import PorterStemmer
nltk.download('punkt', quiet=True)

stemmer = PorterStemmer()

def stem_tokens(tokens):
    """Reduce each word to its root form using Porter Stemmer"""
    return [stemmer.stem(token) for token in tokens]

print("=== STEP 5: Stemming (Porter Stemmer) ===")
stem_examples = [
    "running", "runs", "ran",       # all → "run"
    "learning", "learned", "learns", # all → "learn"
    "analysis", "analyses",          # both → "analysi" (not perfect!)
    "Python", "pythonic",            # "python" → "python", "python" → "python"
]

print(f"{'Original':<15} → {'Stemmed'}")
print("-" * 30)
for word in stem_examples:
    stemmed = stemmer.stem(word.lower())
    print(f"{word:<15} → {stemmed}")
print()

# ── STEP 7: Lemmatisation (smarter than stemming) ─────────────────────

# Lemmatisation uses a dictionary to find the actual base form
# spaCy is the easiest way: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm

print("=== STEP 6: Lemmatisation (spaCy) ===")
try:
    import spacy
    # Load English model (run: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm)
    nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
    
    lemma_examples = ["running", "ran", "better", "geese", "analyses", "children"]
    
    print(f"{'Original':<15} → {'Stemmed (Porter)':<20} → {'Lemmatised (spaCy)'}")
    print("-" * 55)
    for word in lemma_examples:
        stemmed = stemmer.stem(word)
        doc = nlp(word)
        lemma = doc[0].lemma_
        print(f"{word:<15} → {stemmed:<20} → {lemma}")
    print()
    
except OSError:
    print("  (spaCy model not found. Run: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm)")
    print("  Lemmatisation is smarter than stemming — it uses actual dictionaries")
    print("  Example: 'geese' → 'goose' (lemma) vs 'gees' (Porter stem)")
    print()

# ── STEP 8: Full Preprocessing Pipeline ──────────────────────────────

print("=== FULL PREPROCESSING PIPELINE ===")

def full_preprocess_pipeline(text, stop_words=None, use_stemming=True):
    """
    Complete preprocessing pipeline:
    raw text → lowercase → remove punctuation → tokenise → 
    remove stopwords → stem
    """
    # Stage 1: Lowercase
    text = text.lower()
    
    # Stage 2: Handle hyphens (machine-learning → machine learning)
    text = text.replace('-', ' ')
    
    # Stage 3: Remove punctuation
    text = text.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
    
    # Stage 4: Tokenise
    tokens = text.split()
    
    # Stage 5: Remove stopwords (optional)
    if stop_words:
        tokens = [t for t in tokens if t not in stop_words]
    
    # Stage 6: Stem (optional)
    if use_stemming:
        tokens = [stemmer.stem(t) for t in tokens]
    
    return tokens

# Apply to our documents
documents = [
    "Python is great for machine learning and data science",
    "Java is used for enterprise software development",
    "Python and Java are both popular programming languages",
    "Machine learning requires lots of data and computation",
    "Data science uses Python for statistical analysis and modeling"
]

print("Pipeline results (with stopword removal + stemming):")
for i, doc in enumerate(documents):
    raw_tokens    = tokenise_regex(doc)
    preprocessed  = full_preprocess_pipeline(doc, stop_words=stop_words, use_stemming=True)
    print(f"  Doc {i}:")
    print(f"    Raw:         {raw_tokens}")
    print(f"    Preprocessed:{preprocessed}")
    print()

# ── STEP 9: BM25 with Full Preprocessing ─────────────────────────────

from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi

# Build BM25 with preprocessed tokens
preprocessed_docs = [
    full_preprocess_pipeline(doc, stop_words=stop_words, use_stemming=True)
    for doc in documents
]

bm25_preprocessed = BM25Okapi(preprocessed_docs)

print("=== BM25 Search WITH Preprocessing ===")
# Query is also preprocessed the same way!
raw_query = "analyzing Python scripts for machine learning"
query_tokens = full_preprocess_pipeline(raw_query, stop_words=stop_words, use_stemming=True)
print(f"Raw query:        '{raw_query}'")
print(f"Processed query:  {query_tokens}")
print()

scores = bm25_preprocessed.get_scores(query_tokens)
ranked = sorted(enumerate(scores), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
for rank, (doc_id, score) in enumerate(ranked, 1):
    if score > 0:
        print(f"  Rank {rank}: Doc {doc_id} (score={score:.4f}) → '{documents[doc_id]}'")
```

**Expected Output (excerpt):**
```
=== STEP 5: Stemming (Porter Stemmer) ===
Original        → Stemmed
------------------------------
running         → run
runs            → run
ran             → ran      ← Porter can't fix irregular verbs!
learning        → learn
learned         → learn
analysis        → analysi  ← Not perfect
Python          → python
pythonic        → python

=== Lemmatisation (spaCy) ===
Original        → Stemmed (Porter)    → Lemmatised (spaCy)
-------------------------------------------------------
running         → run                 → run
ran             → ran                 → run   ← Correct!
better          → better              → good  ← Handles irregular!
geese           → gees                → goose ← Correct!
```

sections.title: ⑥ Common Beginner Mistakes
sections.body:
❌ **Mistake 1:** Removing stopwords blindly — breaks queries like "not working", "to be or not to be"
✅ **Fix:** Only remove stopwords if your use case genuinely doesn't need them (e.g., factual document search)

❌ **Mistake 2:** Stemming proper nouns — "Apple" → "appl", "Google" → "googl"
✅ **Fix:** Detect and preserve proper nouns, or use lemmatisation with NER instead of stemming

❌ **Mistake 3:** Preprocessing documents but NOT queries with the same pipeline
✅ **Fix:** ALWAYS apply identical preprocessing to both documents and queries

❌ **Mistake 4:** Using stemming for multilingual content — Porter Stemmer is English-only
✅ **Fix:** Use language-specific stemmers or multilingual lemmatisers (spaCy supports 70+ languages)

❌ **Mistake 5:** Removing numbers during preprocessing when they matter (product codes, versions)
✅ **Fix:** Keep numbers if your domain uses them (e.g., "Python 3.10", "model A4512")

sections.title: ⑦ Quick Recap
sections.body:
- 🔠 **Lowercase** everything — "Python" and "python" must be identical tokens
- ✂️ **Remove punctuation** — "science," and "science" are different strings without this step
- 🛑 **Stopwords** — optional; remove "the", "is", "and" *only* when they don't affect meaning
- 🌱 **Stemming** — fast, imperfect (Porter Stemmer); collapses variants like running/runs/run
- 🧠 **Lemmatisation** — slower, smarter (spaCy); handles irregular forms like ran→run, geese→goose

sections.title: ⑧ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║              TEXT PREPROCESSING PIPELINE — VISUAL GUIDE              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

 RAW TEXT → BM25-READY TOKENS
 ══════════════════════════════

 Input: "Running Python scripts is EASY! Machine-learning: best practices."

 Stage 1: LOWERCASE
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 "running python scripts is easy! machine-learning: best practices."

 Stage 2: HANDLE HYPHENS
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 "running python scripts is easy! machine learning: best practices."

 Stage 3: REMOVE PUNCTUATION
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 "running python scripts is easy machine learning best practices"

 Stage 4: TOKENISE (split)
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ["running", "python", "scripts", "is", "easy", "machine", "learning", "best", "practices"]

 Stage 5: REMOVE STOPWORDS
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Remove: "is" (stopword)
 ["running", "python", "scripts", "easy", "machine", "learning", "best", "practices"]

 Stage 6: STEM (Porter Stemmer)
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 "running" → "run"      "scripts" → "script"    "learning" → "learn"
 "easy"    → "easi"     "practices"→ "practic"
 ["run", "python", "script", "easi", "machin", "learn", "best", "practic"]

 Output ready for BM25!

 STEMMING vs LEMMATISATION
 ══════════════════════════

 Word         Porter Stemmer          spaCy Lemmatiser
 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 "running"  → "run"          ✅      "run"           ✅
 "ran"      → "ran"          ❌      "run"           ✅  ← lemma wins!
 "better"   → "better"       ❌      "good"          ✅  ← lemma wins!
 "geese"    → "gees"         ❌      "goose"         ✅  ← lemma wins!
 "analysis" → "analysi"      ❌      "analysis"      ✅  ← lemma wins!
 "easily"   → "easili"       ❌      "easily"        ⚠️  (debatable)

 Speed:        Porter: FAST (rule-based)        spaCy: SLOWER (model-based)
 Accuracy:     Porter: moderate                  spaCy: high
 Use when:     Speed critical, English only      Accuracy critical, multilingual

 WHY SAME PIPELINE FOR DOCS AND QUERIES IS CRITICAL
 ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════

 Document stored as: ["run", "python", "script"]   (after stem)
                          ↑
                      "running" → "run"

 If query is NOT preprocessed:
 Query: ["running", "python"]  ← "running" ≠ "run"  → MISS! ❌

 If query IS preprocessed:
 Query: ["run", "python"]      ← "run" == "run"      → MATCH! ✅
```
